target_customer: Retailers and carriers that want to sell devices on subscription; consumers buy through them (the current site also sells a MacBook upgrade plan through partner stores)
problem: Resellers cannot easily run device subscription programs, which need lender integrations and residual value management, so customers upgrade slowly and loyalty is weak.
business_model: B2B infrastructure for device subscription and financing programs, with financing partners

competitors.name: Apple iPhone Upgrade Program
competitors.what: Monthly payment plan with a yearly upgrade and AppleCare+, extended to online sales in April 2016

competitors.name: US carrier installment and upgrade plans
competitors.what: Carrier installment plans that let customers swap phones early, which compete for the same upgrade cycle

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with lenders and retailers and residual value tracking are standard fintech engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Once a retailer or carrier runs its program on the platform it is integrated with lenders and logistics; but the idea can be copied by financiers or Apple itself.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple and carriers already ran their own upgrade programs in 2016. Upgraded later listed Apple, Dixons Elkjop, MediaMarkt and Vodafone as partners on its YC profile, so it partnered rather than being displaced.

market_need_then: Apple launched its upgrade program in 2015 and carriers followed with installment plans, showing consumers wanted upgrade-anytime pricing; the YC profile cites US carrier financing growing from $13B to $51B in four years.

branding.domain_note: Uses getupgraded.com, a prefix domain; the exact upgraded.com was not found to be owned.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer copy such as get a new MacBook every two years

brand_strength.rationale: A generic common word shared with many firms called Upgrade; no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Upgraded remained active as of 2026 with a small team of about 13, partners including Apple resellers and Vodafone per its YC profile, and a consumer MacBook subscription offering on its site. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was found. With no verified funding and a crowded space where Apple and carriers run their own programs, its trajectory looks like a modest B2B infrastructure business rather than a breakout.
notes: Funding unverified: StartupIntros lists a $1M seed (2016-08) and a $2M seed (2018-12), VCBacked says $750K total, CB Insights shows $120K; these conflict and are aggregators only, so no round is recorded. No Series A found. The company site and YC page name no prior employers or education for the founders. The current site does not mention founders or funding.
